name: Oregon
reason: HB 2001 (2019): duplexes in cities 10,000–25,000 from 2021-06-30; 2–4 homes in cities 25,000+ and Metro from 2022-06-30. Before 2015–2019, after 2023–2025. Every reporting place in the state counts, Portland included.

name: California
reason: SB 9 (2021): 2 homes per lot and lot splits in single-family zones from 2022-01-01. Before 2018–2021, after 2023–2025. Every reporting place counts, Sacramento included. Read as California's 2022 package (other housing laws at the same time).

name: Maine
reason: LD 2003 (2022): 2 homes per lot, up to 4 in growth areas, from 2024 (council towns 2024-01-01, others 2024-07-01). Before 2019–2023, after 2024–2025.

name: Vermont
reason: Act 47 (2023): duplexes wherever homes are allowed, up to 4 homes where water and sewer serve, from 2023-07-01. Before 2019–2022, after 2024–2025.

name: Places in the four states that did not report every month
reason: Left out: a place counts only if it reported all 12 months in every before and after year and has at least 100 single-family homes.

name: West: Idaho, Wyoming, Alaska, Nevada, New Mexico
reason: Same Census region as Oregon and California, no state law of the screened kinds 2015–2025. Each law place is compared with places ½ to 2 times its population. West pool is thin.

name: Northeast: Pennsylvania, New York, New Jersey
reason: Same Census region as Maine and Vermont, no state law of the screened kinds 2015–2025.

name: California matches
reason: Places with no comparison place at ½ to 2 times their population are left unmatched (not compared nationally in the main result).

name: Washington, Montana, Arizona
reason: Own state middle-housing laws, binding 2024 or later. Too new to test; never comparisons.

name: Massachusetts, Colorado, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Utah, New Hampshire
reason: Own state housing laws of the screened kinds (ADUs, upzoning near transit, parking) binding 2015–2025, so not a clean comparison.

name: Texas, Florida, Maryland
reason: Own state housing laws: Texas SB 840 and SB 15 (2025-09-01), Florida Live Local Act (2023-07-01), Maryland HB 538 (2024).

name: 24 cities and boroughs outside the law states
reason: Their own local reform of the same kinds 2015–2025, or a city studied separately: Anchorage, Boise, Chicago, Minneapolis, St. Paul, Reno, Trenton, New York's 5 boroughs, Buffalo, Durham, Raleigh, Mecklenburg County, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Austin, Houston, Alexandria, Arlington County, Spokane, Walla Walla. Never comparisons.

name: Places in counties bordering Oregon or California
reason: Next door to a law state, so builders may cross the line. Never comparisons.

name: 34 states that pass the screen
reason: Used only to test the result: 10,000 sets of 4 fake law states, each compared the same way.
